## Corrected {#corrected}

The first version of this article, published on 30 October 2026, was written from WIRED's posts and six outlets, because WIRED's page could not be fetched from here. Later that day I read the article itself, and it showed two things the shadow had wrong, which this article repeated:

• **A quote given to the wrong party.** "We take all concerns seriously" is the first sentence of Accenture's statement, not the end of the DOD's. One outlet joined it to the DOD's line, and we copied it.

• **Commits.** The detail that the agent "committed" code on the employee's behalf came from secondary coverage; WIRED's own text, in the part I have read, says the setup was to let the agent "write and deploy code".

Both are corrected above, and the [version history](../the-contractors-agent-and-three-policies.md) shows the change. It is a small, useful lesson for the shadow method: the shadow is evidence, and it can also carry a quote across a paragraph break.
